The monarchs also reaffirmed their unwavering support for President Bola Tinubu and his administration while backing the proposed establishment of state police as part of efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s security architecture. In a communiqué issued and read by the Alake of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Gbadebo, at the end of the meeting, said the rotational presidency arrangement had contributed significantly to political stability, inclusiveness and national cohesion, stressing that the arrangement should be sustained in the next electoral cycle. top.title: 2027: SDP inaugurates 12,000-member campaign council, names Tanko coordinator
top.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) has inaugurated a 12,000-member Presidential Campaign Council, PCC, with Dr Yunusa Tanko appointed as its National Coordinator. The SDP National Chairman, Professor Sadiq Gombe, who will also serve as chairman of the council, inaugurated the campaign council on Wednesday in Abuja. Gombe charged members of the council to work towards securing electoral victory for the party, stressing that its campaign must be issue-based, people-centred and guided by the provisions of the Constitution, the Electoral Act, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) guidelines and the party’s constitution. He urged members to approach the election with the seriousness it deserved, adding that the party was determined to challenge President Bola Tinubu at the polls. “Let us approach this election with the seriousness it deserves to unseat President Tinubu. “Our campaign must be issue-based, people-centred and firmly rooted in the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, the Electoral Act, INEC guidelines and our party constitution. “We must earn the confidence of Nigerians through credible engagement, persuasion, effective organisation and practical policy alternatives. “We must reject violence, intimidation, electoral malpractice and every conduct capable of undermining the integrity of our democracy,” he said. The SDP chairman described Nigeria as being at a critical crossroads, citing insecurity, economic hardship, unemployment, poverty, institutional weaknesses and declining public confidence in governance as some of the challenges confronting the country. According to him, Nigerians are yearning for purposeful leadership, economic opportunities, social justice, security and accountability, as well as a government that prioritises their welfare and dignity. He said the SDP was determined to provide Nigerians with a credible democratic alternative founded on social justice, equity, freedom, inclusive development and good governance. Gombe urged members of the campaign council to take the party’s message to communities across the country, engage citizens respectfully, listen to their concerns and demonstrate through their conduct that the party deserved their confidence. He further charged the council to ensure that the party’s campaign remained peaceful, credible and focused on offering practical solutions to the country’s challenges. top.title: Russia’s Central Bank Clears Exchange to Open Bitcoin and Crypto Trading on Nov. 22
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s Central Bank Clears Exchange to Open Bitcoin and Crypto Trading on Nov. 22 The Bank of Russia said Wednesday that exchanges may start organized trading in cryptocurrencies on Nov. 22, once the central bank has approved their trading rules, a step that lands just ahead of Moscow Exchange’s planned Dec. 1 bitcoin launch. The ordinance, which amends the Bank of Russia’s rules for organized trading, was registered by the Justice Ministry on Nov. 3 and published Wednesday on the regulator’s site. It takes effect 10 days after publication, on Nov. 22. Exchanges will have to register the brokers, trust managers and central counterparties that take part in crypto trades, keep registers of orders and deals, and monitor the activity. They must also calculate a current price, a weighted-average price, a market price and a closing price, and report trading activity to the central bank in the same way they already do for other assets. The regulator was clear about the order of operations. Exchanges may open crypto markets from Nov. 22, it said, “but first they must agree with the regulator on the rules for conducting such trading.” It did not say whether any venue has already cleared that review. Who can buy, and what they can buy A separate ordinance, published Nov. 6 and due to take effect Nov. 17, sets the menu for ordinary buyers. The Bank of Russia approved bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT for purchase by non-qualified investors, and said exchanges may admit those assets to public trading from that date. Non-qualified investors can buy through a broker, a trust manager or a registered crypto exchange office, on an exchange or over the counter. Purchases through a single intermediary may not exceed 300,000 rubles a year, roughly $3,600 at the official exchange rate. Qualified investors can access all cryptoassets with no purchase cap. Both groups still have to pass a knowledge test and read a risk disclosure before they can trade. The list is limited to the most liquid assets that meet the law’s tests for market capitalization, average daily volume and at least five years of pricing history on foreign exchanges. Moscow Exchange still aims for Dec. 1 Moscow Exchange, Russia’s largest trading venue, announced on Nov. 2 that it plans to offer bitcoin, ether and USDT trades from Dec. 1, initially as a pilot while participants connect. Trading would run on its existing stock-market systems from 6:50 a.m. to 11:50 p.m. Moscow time, with the National Clearing Centre clearing the deals and clients able to settle the same day or the next. Bitcoin Magazine reported the Dec. 1 plan last week, including the U.S. sanctions that already cover the exchange and its clearing house. Boris Blokhin, a senior managing director at the exchange, said in early October that Moscow Exchange would not need additional licenses to start and would use a partner settlement digital depository. top.title: Obi prefers ‘anywhere food is ready politics’ – Wike
top.description: Says, Atiku won’t get 25% across South By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC, Mr Peter Obi, prefers “anywhere food is ready politics”. Wike spoke on Tuesday when he met youth stakeholders in the FCT to campaign for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in the January presidential election. “Obi is not going anywhere. Don’t deceive yourself. If he likes, let him enter the motorcycle and carry everybody at the back; he is not going anywhere,” the minister said. He mocked Obi’s visits to camps for internally displaced persons (IDPs). ” He goes to IDP camp to do birthdays. When he was governor, did he do that? No. Very soon, they will start going along the trees, buying and chewing corn. “He prefers anywhere Mama Put is ready for politics. He doesn’t want to struggle. Small fight, he ran away from the PDP. He did the same in the Labour Party, and now he is in NDC. But, as for me, I am not afraid of fighting. They have now run away from the PDP, and I am still in the party,” he said. The minister also dismissed the chances of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, the African Democratic Congress ADC presidential candidate. “Atiku won’t get 25 per cent in South South, South East and South West. Where will he get it?” he asked. He urged the youths to do more than vote for Tinubu. “Please, I beg of you, not to just come out to vote, not to just endorse this president here, mobilise all your colleagues, even those who are not part of your association, reach out to them, and get everybody to come out. “I am not a member of the All Progressives Congress. You don’t need to be an APC member or a Peoples Democratic Party PDP member for you to contribute to the development of your country. All you need to do is to work according to the vision of the person who has appointed you. Let’s not put our destiny in the hands of political gamblers who have been gambling for over 22 years,” he said. Wike reminded the youths of the record of earlier administrations on their welfare and that of women in the FCT. “Atiku Abubakar was vice president from 1999 to 2007. Is it not correct? Correct. Was there any establishment of a youth secretariat? No. Was there any establishment of a women’s secretariat? No. From 1976 to 2023, nobody cared,” he added. He said Tinubu changed that within a year of taking office. “Go and make sure there is a youth secretary. Go and make sure there’s a woman secretary,” he quoted the president as directing. He urged the youths to ignore showmanship. “Leave all these rhetorics; leave all this drama. These are cosmetic. Let us face the reality on the ground. That is what matters,” he said. top.description: Free agent pitcher Tarik Skubal If not for an impending lockout, Tarik Skubal's free agency would have every headline in baseball this offseason. The two-time Cy Young Award winner is set up to sign a record-breaking contract in the coming weeks, and according to ESPN's Jeff Passan, Skubal wants to not only get paid, but he wants a lengthy deal. "Certainly the Dodgers will be in the mix on Skubal, but to what extent is unclear," wrote Passan on Wednesday. "Unlike Kyle Tucker last offseason, Skubal has no interest in a shorter-term, higher-dollar deal, which could disadvantage the Dodgers when contending with the New York Mets (or the San Diego Padres or Toronto Blue Jays)." The Dodgers have excelled at signing players to deals with deferred money or short deals with high total value. However, it's not like they cannot dish out longer contracts. They did so for Mookie Betts, Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman and Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! However, with everything going on with Mark Walter outside of baseball right now, it may be a little more difficult for them to dish out a double-digit-year deal. However, it's not impossible. At the end of the day, they are still the Dodgers and should be able to compete with anyone financially. However, they are coming off a sweep in the National League Championship Series in which their offense disappeared. They won back-to-back World Series with weaker rotations than the one they trotted out in October this year, and they need to evaluate if spending big on Skubal is really what they need. “He was awesome to get to know,’’ Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes said on Tuesday, per USA Today's Bob Nightengale. “He fit in great into the clubhouse. Obviously, we know what kind of pitcher he is. So, for us, it’s understanding what this all looks like, as far as what does our team need? What does the contract look like? Where does he end up? I don’t know.’’ The Dodgers may not think it's the best idea to sign Skubal to a long-term deal, and if that's what he desires, the Dodgers will really have to hope the allure of winning can get him to change his mind. top.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
top.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. top.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
top.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. top.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram

Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. The Frenchman was recently elevated to undisputed champion after Tom Aspinall vacated the title due to further complications with his eye injury. However, much of the attention surrounding the Madison Square Garden headliner has focused on Gane’s legitimacy as champion and the growing criticism of his illegal tactics inside the Octagon. While the Frenchman has pushed back against accusations of being a dirty fighter, he recently made another revealing admission ahead of his showdown. Gane opened up about his defeat to Jon Jones at UFC 285 , describing the experience as a major turning point in his career. The reigning champion also reflected on how the loss affected his confidence and changed his mindset as a fighter. Ciryl Gane Explains How His UFC 285 Loss to Jon Jones Fueled His Comeback At UFC 285 in March 2023, Jones made his long-awaited heavyweight debut after nearly four years away from competition. He challenged Gane for the vacant heavyweight championship, with the Frenchman entering the contest fresh off a knockout victory over Tai Tuivasa at UFC Paris. Many expected Gane to provide Jones with a difficult test, considering the latter was moving up a division and returning after an extended layoff. However, the fight unfolded very differently. Despite taking an early groin strike, Jones quickly took control of the contest, secured a takedown and locked in a guillotine choke. Gane was forced to tap in less than three minutes, handing Jones his second UFC championship. Speaking in a recent interview with UFC on Paramount+ , Gane reflected on the defeat and said, “I think it was after the Jon Jones loss because it was a real loss.” Although Gane had already suffered his first professional MMA defeat against Francis Ngannou at UFC 270, that fight went the distance, with the Cameroonian winning by unanimous decision. The loss to Jones, however, was a much more decisive setback. Gane explained, “The fight against Francis Ngannou was a little bit square, but after Jon Jones, something changed in my mindset because also the pressure of social media from everywhere.” The 36-year-old further opened up about the criticism he received and the doubts he had about continuing his career. He added, “Like, ‘Ciryl Gane, we overestimated him,’ blah, blah, blah. I was disappointed. It was 2023, and I started MMA in 2019, so I already did pretty much in four years. One side of my head was about to give my back to everyone, but because I’m a competitor and because I want to prove to myself, I’m going to stay. I’m going to prove to myself.'” Since that setback, Gane has remained unbeaten, defeating Alexander Volkov at UFC 310 before earning another heavyweight title opportunity against Aspinall at UFC 321

The 82-time PGA Tour winner said he is “training quite a bit” and “feeling better” nearly eight months after he last played competitive golf and then, days later, was arrested and charged with a DUI in Florida. “I’m feeling better, no doubt about that,” Woods, 50, told Sirius XM PGA Tour Radio in an interview that aired Tuesday, Nov. 10. “I’ve been training quite a bit. I will be at Hero [World Challenge]. I’m there either way, so I’ll see you there.” Woods is set to host the no-cut, 72-hole tournament in the Bahamas, which begins on Dec. 3 with a 20-man field. Tiger Woods in February at the 2026 Genesis Invitational Golf Tournament. Credit: Javier Rojas/PI via ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock The legendary golfer is also expected to compete in Jupiter Links GC’s season-opener on Dec. 27, and could return to the PNC Championship, which he has historically played with his son, Charlie , according to ESPN, After rupturing his Achilles tendon in March 2025 and undergoing extensive rehab, Woods was on the cusp of playing in the Masters this past April, but that comeback ended with his March 27 arrest. Woods was arrested after he rolled over his Range Rover in a two-car accident in Jupiter Island, Fla. In an affidavit obtained by PEOPLE at the time, deputies with the Martin County Sheriff’s Office found two hydrocodone pills in Woods’ left pants pocket while at the scene. Woods apologized and underwent treatment in Switzerland amid the news that his girlfriend, Vanessa Trump , had been diagnosed with breast cancer. top.title: ICE and OKX Set Nov. 23 Tokenized Stock Launch After 67 Companies Opt Out
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine ICE and OKX Set Nov. 23 Tokenized Stock Launch After 67 Companies Opt Out OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) will open their tokenized stock venue on Nov. 23, the companies said Wednesday, offering more than 70 assets under a temporary SEC exemption even as 67 companies, including Apple, Tesla and Meta, have already objected. The OKX announcement said more than 70 assets are expected to be listed, including securities from Better.com, BitGo, Circle, Coinbase, Robinhood, Securitize and Strategy (MSTR), as well as 59 exchange-traded funds from Direxion. Strategy will also list its preferred stocks, such as STRC. Access at launch is limited to eligible U.S. customers of OKX Inc. who have activated a CeDeFi Wallet, passed identity checks and completed onboarding with the joint venture, which is called OKXICE and is owned equally by ICE and OKC USA Holding Inc., an OKX affiliate. Trading will run around the clock in the OKX app. “The future of finance is onchain, and we have an opportunity to build it here in America, with the standards, safeguards and ambition that investors expect,” said former New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo, who co-chairs OKXICE with Trabue Bland. The companies did not say how many of the more than 70 assets will trade on the first day, or how much liquidity the pools will have at the open. The venue is not a registered exchange or broker-dealer and is not approved by the SEC, the announcement said. How the venue will work Trading will run through automated market maker pools built on Uniswap v4 and deployed on X Layer, the Ethereum layer-2 network OKX operates. Only approved wallets can trade or add liquidity. Securitize will provide the tokenization infrastructure. Each token represents a security entitlement backed one-for-one by a U.S. share held by a registered broker-dealer, and holders keep the usual shareholder rights, including dividends, voting and corporate actions, the venue said in a Nov. 5 public notice required under the exemption. Customers will hold the tokens in their own wallets. OKXICE will not hold the assets or the private keys. The tokens will be paired with payment stablecoins such as USDC and USDG. The venue does not operate an order book, does not extend credit and does not conduct primary offerings, the notice said. 67 companies have already opted out The same Nov. 5 notice lists 67 issuers that had sent a written objection by that date, among them Apple, Amazon, Tesla, Meta, Netflix, Nvidia, Microsoft, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Costco, Nike and Home Depot. The list has grown from 50 objectors in an Oct. 30 notice. The objections stem from the SEC’s five-year “Innovation Exemption,” issued Sept. 17, which lets tokenized securities venues trade blockchain versions of U.S. stocks through automated market makers without registering as exchanges. top.title: 'Need to find a replacement': Irfan Pathan identifies Punjab Kings' weak link after blockbuster Hardik-Arshdeep exchange
top.description: The blockbuster trade between Mumbai Indians (MI) and Punjab Kings (PBKS) has triggered plenty of discussion around the possible playing combinations of both franchises ahead of IPL 2027. While Punjab have strengthened their batting with the arrival of Indian all-rounder Hardik Pandya, they have also parted ways with one of their most dependable fast bowlers, Arshdeep Singh. Former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan has weighed in on the high-profile exchange, highlighting the benefits of Hardik's arrival for Punjab while raising concerns over their bowling resources following Arshdeep's departure. Taking to X, Pathan pointed out that Hardik's addition would provide Punjab with a much-needed power-hitting option in the middle and lower order. "With this trade of Hardik, Punjab get a really good middle and lower order power hitter. Their batting line-up was already strong, but this makes them even stronger in that department. "Their bowling is a real concern for me. They not only need to find a replacement for Arshdeep Singh but also need to invest in a good spinner going forward," Pathan wrote. — IrfanPathan (@IrfanPathan) Hardik Pandya joins Punjab Kings in blockbuster trade The trade sees Hardik return to a new franchise after his second stint with Mumbai Indians, while Arshdeep brings his seven-year association with Punjab Kings to an end. Hardik will join Punjab Kings for a fee of Rs 18 crore, up from his previous retention fee of Rs 16.35 crore. Arshdeep, meanwhile, will move to Mumbai Indians at his existing fee of Rs 18 crore. Hardik's arrival adds considerable experience and firepower to Punjab's batting unit. The all-rounder has featured in 162 IPL matches, scoring 2,955 runs at a strike rate of 146.28 while picking up 82 wickets. However, Arshdeep's departure leaves a significant gap in Punjab's bowling attack. The left-arm pacer was the franchise's leading wicket-taker, claiming 111 wickets in 96 IPL appearances. His ability to provide breakthroughs with the new ball and deliver at the death made him a crucial part of the team's bowling combination. 135737338 Irfan Pathan explains how Arshdeep's arrival benefits Mumbai Indians Earlier, Pathan had also highlighted how the acquisition of Arshdeep could significantly strengthen Mumbai Indians' bowling attack. "The trade of Arshdeep Singh makes Mumbai Indians a much stronger side. It allows them to use Jasprit Bumrah even more effectively and also has a positive impact on their overseas slots," he wrote on X. — IrfanPathan (@IrfanPathan) Arshdeep's arrival gives Mumbai another reliable Indian fast-bowling option alongside Jasprit Bumrah and Deepak Chahar. The five-time champions also have left-arm pacer Trent Boult and young Indian bowler Ashwani Kumar in their pace-bowling department.

top.title: Kenyon Martin Defends LeBron James For Helping Bronny Reach The NBA Despite Not Being Ready
top.description: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Kenyon Martin believes Bronny James entered the NBA a year too soon. He still understands why LeBron James would use his influence to help his son get there. In Martin’s view, any parent in LeBron’s position would do the same, even if Bronny would have benefited from another season at USC. Speaking on the TFU podcast , Martin addressed the criticism that has followed Bronny since the Los Angeles Lakers selected him with the No. 55 pick in the 2024 NBA Draft. Martin said that he did not question the influence of James’ name, but he also questioned why parents would pass on the chance to influence their own child’s future. “With Bronny and LeBron, yes, nepotism is real. We all know it and we all would do it. If we had the opportunity to do it, 1000%. If any one of us are able to put our child in a position to succeed and have direct influence on it, we would. No doubt about it.” “Do I think Bronny at the time was ready for the NBA? No. Because of his lack of college experience that he had. It was interrupted because of the heart thing. Would loved to have seen him at USC another year to just get playing time. Get used to being back on the floor without all the pressures of what came with making that decision to being in the NBA, and your last name being James.” “And without all the pressures and scrutiny of everything that came with being the 55th pick in the NBA draft, which no other 55th pick has those kind of expectations. We get it. His last name is James, but it’s unfair to the kid. He’s still a kid. But it’s their family. It’s their decision and wish them nothing but the best.” Bronny suffered a cardiac arrest at a USC practice before the season even began. He returned to play 25 games, starting six, averaging 4.8 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 2.1 assists. Martin did say that he would have wanted Bronny to spend another year at USC and get regular minutes to find his rhythm before dealing with the attention that came with joining his father in Los Angeles. The attention obviously cuts both ways. Being LeBron’s son gave Bronny a chance that most prospects won’t even have, but it has also meant that every shot can come under the microscope, whether in the NBA or not. Most No. 55 picks get to develop before being expected to contribute off the bench. Bronny never had that luxury. Now in his third season, the 22-year-old is yet to secure a regular rotation role in JJ Redick’s lineup. Through his first five NBA appearances this season, he’s averaged just 0.8 points. But in his return to the G League this season , he did look far more like himself and was comfortable. He put up 22 points, five rebounds, and seven assists as the South Bay Lakers won 104-98 over the Salt Lake City Stars. One strong G League game won’t mean that Bronny will earn a day-to-day spot, but it just shows why playing time still matters. top.title: Malik Nabers Shuts Down Broadcast Critics With Raw Honesty
top.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Malik Nabers refused to let a TV crew define his character after Sunday’s win. The Giants wide receiver called the broadcast critique a “lie” and said he will keep speaking his mind. Calling Out the Narrative Fox play-by-play man Joe Davis and analyst Greg Olsen spent time talking about Nabers during the game. They pointed to his reaction on the sideline and claimed his body language was poor. Nabers saw this on social media and decided to strike back. “I just feel like the narrative on me is always all the bad body language things that people have been saying,” Nabers said in comments reported by the New York Post . He said he will not change his behavior to please strangers watching from home. The criticism came after a tough first half where the Giants struggled to score. Nabers spiked his helmet when his team only managed field goals. His streak of four straight 100-yard games ended in that contest, leaving him with 43 yards on five catches. “One thing about it is that I’m an ultimate competitor whether it’s going [well] or if it’s going bad,” Nabers told reporters per the New York Post. He said his intense style comes from a deep passion for the sport, not anger, and he expects others to share that passion. A Direct Challenge to Olsen The former NFL tight end Greg Olsen suggested Nabers was unhappy for teammate Isaiah Likely after a touchdown. Olsen implied Nabers was not a good teammate because of how he carried himself on the field. Nabers rejected this idea entirely and said he has never been called a bad teammate before. “I feel like that was just a lie, attacking my character as a football player and as a teammate,” Nabers stated according to ESPN . He noted that he holds everyone to a high standard of playing “mean” and getting the team fired up. Nabers said he would welcome a simple conversation with Olsen if the analyst wants to talk. He wants to clear the air but will not apologize for his competitiveness. “If he wants to reach out, he can reach out. We can have a civil conversation,” Nabers said per the New York Post. The Giants star emphasized that no one else can speak for him, so he must use his own voice to set the record straight. Focus Shifts to Washington The Giants (5-2-1) hold first place in their division after beating the Eagles 19-11. Nabers said he is already moving past the broadcast drama to focus on the next opponent. He mentioned that the long year of rehab he endured to return from a torn ACL, fuels his drive this season. The team now prepares for a Thursday night game against the Washington Commanders. That matchup is set for Thursday, Nov. 12, at 8:15 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium.

top.title: Kane says England appearance record a 'testament to dedication'
top.description: Harry Kane will set a new England record of 126 appearances when he features in a Nations League match against Croatia at Wembley (John Walton) England captain Harry Kane said breaking the Three Lions' appearance record in Thursday's Nations League clash with Croatia will represent a "testament to all the dedication" that has gone into his career. When Kane leads England out at Wembley to earn his 126th cap, he will surpass the previous record held by former goalkeeper Peter Shilton since 1990. It will be the latest landmark in an incredible 12 months for the Bayern Munich striker, who in October became the first English player in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or. The 33-year-old Kane is also England's record scorer with 91 goals, as well as holding Tottenham Hotspur's all-time mark with 280. Since leaving Spurs to join Bayern in 2023, Kane has taken his game to another level. He has amassed 156 goals for the German club, finally winning the first silverware of his career with Bundesliga titles in 2025 and 2026. But breaking Shilton's long-standing record also matters to Kane, who told a pre-match press conference on Wednesday: "It's definitely up there as the biggest (achievement). "I think it showcases consistency at the highest level. Testament to all the dedication, the time people don't see that keeps me fit and healthy. This is one of the biggest milestones in my career." For all Kane's brilliance, England have not won a major men's international trophy since lifting the 1966 World Cup on home soil. And Kane suffered fresh frustration in July as England were beaten by Argentina in the semi-finals of the World Cup. - 'Beautiful occasion' - England were leading 1-0 until late in the game but could not score again, with manager Thomas Tuchel criticised for packing the team's defence only for Argentina to score twice late on as Kane was denied a first appearance in a World Cup final. "In terms of what's next, I don't like to put limits -- 100 goals (for England) is a milestone to reach as soon as possible," added Kane. "We've done extremely well in tournaments, going into latter stages. I'm feeling really good and hopefully there will be many more years to see what I can achieve." Tuchel, speaking earlier Wednesday, was coy when asked if Kane was England's greatest footballer. "I don't know. He's up there of course. It's now proven. It's always nice if things are proven in sports -- he has his prizes and records, he will build on these records, score more goals and get more games. "Tomorrow he will start for us and as captain. It's a big occasion to present the Ballon d'Or trophy to our fans and have it embedded in the same day he gets his all-time record for 126 matches, it's a beautiful occasion." England are all but guaranteed a place in March's Nations League quarter-finals, regardless of Thursday's result, having thrashed Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka last month in what Tuchel labelled a "freak result". The monarchs also reaffirmed their unwavering support for President Bola Tinubu and his administration while backing the proposed establishment of state police as part of efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s security architecture. nigeria.title: 2027: SDP inaugurates 12,000-member campaign council, names Tanko coordinator
nigeria.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) has inaugurated a 12,000-member Presidential Campaign Council, PCC, with Dr Yunusa Tanko appointed as its National Coordinator. The SDP National Chairman, Professor Sadiq Gombe, who will also serve as chairman of the council, inaugurated the campaign council on Wednesday in Abuja. Gombe charged members of the council to work towards securing electoral victory for the party, stressing that its campaign must be issue-based, people-centred and guided by the provisions of the Constitution, the Electoral Act, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) guidelines and the party’s constitution. He urged members to approach the election with the seriousness it deserved, adding that the party was determined to challenge President Bola Tinubu at the polls. “Let us approach this election with the seriousness it deserves to unseat President Tinubu. “Our campaign must be issue-based, people-centred and firmly rooted in the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, the Electoral Act, INEC guidelines and our party constitution. “We must earn the confidence of Nigerians through credible engagement, persuasion, effective organisation and practical policy alternatives. “We must reject violence, intimidation, electoral malpractice and every conduct capable of undermining the integrity of our democracy,” he said. nigeria.title: Nigeria’s crude oil output drops to 1.51m bpd in October — NUPRC
nigeria.description: Nigeria’s crude oil production declined slightly to 1.51 million barrels per day (bpd) in October 2026, from 1.53 million bpd recorded in September, according to data from the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC). The figure represents a 1.7 per cent month-on-month decline. Despite the drop, Nigeria maintained crude oil production above its Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) quota of 1.5 million bpd for the sixth consecutive month in 2026. OPEC data showed that Nigeria produced 1.5 million bpd in August, 1.50 million bpd in July, 1.55 million bpd in June and 1.53 million bpd in May. When condensates are included, the country’s average daily production stood at 1.68 million barrels in October. NUPRC data also showed that daily production peaked at 1.79 million barrels during the month, while the lowest output was 1.60 million barrels per day. The commission attributed the relatively stable production levels in recent months to improved operational stability, production uptime and crude evacuation efficiency. “The sustained growth recorded in October reflects the continued commitment of operators and industry stakeholders towards improving operational efficiency, maintaining asset integrity, and enhancing production reliability across the Nigerian upstream petroleum sector,” the commission said. A breakdown of daily average crude oil and condensate production by terminals and streams showed that Forcados recorded the highest output at 318,490 barrels per day, followed by Bonny Terminal with 311,020 bpd. Qua Iboe Terminal recorded an average production of 173,970 bpd, while Escravos Oil Terminal posted a daily average of 134,670 bpd. The commission added that Bonga ranked as the fifth-highest producing terminal, recording an average of 106,650 bpd of crude oil and condensate. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s Central Bank Clears Exchange to Open Bitcoin and Crypto Trading on Nov. 22 The Bank of Russia said Wednesday that exchanges may start organized trading in cryptocurrencies on Nov. 22, once the central bank has approved their trading rules, a step that lands just ahead of Moscow Exchange’s planned Dec. 1 bitcoin launch. The ordinance, which amends the Bank of Russia’s rules for organized trading, was registered by the Justice Ministry on Nov. 3 and published Wednesday on the regulator’s site. It takes effect 10 days after publication, on Nov. 22. Exchanges will have to register the brokers, trust managers and central counterparties that take part in crypto trades, keep registers of orders and deals, and monitor the activity. They must also calculate a current price, a weighted-average price, a market price and a closing price, and report trading activity to the central bank in the same way they already do for other assets. The regulator was clear about the order of operations. Exchanges may open crypto markets from Nov. 22, it said, “but first they must agree with the regulator on the rules for conducting such trading.” It did not say whether any venue has already cleared that review. The Bank of Russia approved bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT for purchase by non-qualified investors, and said exchanges may admit those assets to public trading from that date. Non-qualified investors can buy through a broker, a trust manager or a registered crypto exchange office, on an exchange or over the counter. Purchases through a single intermediary may not exceed 300,000 rubles a year, roughly $3,600 at the official exchange rate. Qualified investors can access all cryptoassets with no purchase cap. Both groups still have to pass a knowledge test and read a risk disclosure before they can trade. The list is limited to the most liquid assets that meet the law’s tests for market capitalization, average daily volume and at least five years of pricing history on foreign exchanges. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Deutsche Bank Switches On Bitcoin Custody for Paying Clients Deutsche Bank has switched on its digital asset custody service for paying clients, the German lender said Wednesday, letting institutions and corporations in Europe hold bitcoin with the country’s largest bank less than two months after it first unveiled the plan. The bank announced the service on Sept. 16, saying it would go live with first clients this year once regulators signed off. It now supports bitcoin and ether, along with the USDC, EURC and EURAU stablecoins, according to its product page . Under the setup, Deutsche Bank manages the wallets and private keys on behalf of clients, who can store the assets and transfer them to third parties. The bank pitched that as a way for clients to skip building and maintaining their own custody infrastructure. “In the medium term we aim to deliver a fully integrated, regulated ecosystem that supports the custody, tokenisation, and settlement of digital assets,” said Paul Maley, global head of trust and securities services at Deutsche Bank. The bank did not name its first clients, say how many have signed up or disclose what it charges to hold the coins. The service is aimed at institutional and corporate clients, not retail customers. What Deutsche Bank is offering The product page describes private keys stored in hardware security modules, a choice of warm and cold storage, multi-factor authentication, segregation of client assets and a customizable approval process for client transfers. Clients reach the service through Autobahn, Deutsche Bank’s multi-channel gateway, or its Corporate Bank portal. The service is booked out of Deutsche Bank AG in Frankfurt and is available in Germany, with cross-border servicing across Europe through passporting. The bank lists institutional investors, multinationals and corporates, governments and sovereigns, and wealth managers as target clients, and it describes the offering as compliant with the European Union’s MiCA crypto rules. For now the menu is narrow. Deutsche lists custody, transfers and internal moves between warm and cold storage as its initial services, with “further capabilities planned.” The September release said the asset list may grow with client demand and that tokenized financial instruments are on the roadmap. entertainment.description: Two people engaging with technology in a contemporary hotel lobby work setting. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing how people learn, work, communicate and solve problems. In today’s world, if you’re not on board with AI, it could be said you’re being resistant to the fastest-growing technological innovation in the world. From students researching academic subjects to professionals developing business ideas, AI tools have become companions in everyday activities for people. They can help save time, explore new ideas, understand difficult concepts and approach tasks differently. However, as more people embrace these AI tools, it is important to understand that using AI effectively goes beyond knowing what prompts to enter. It requires knowing when to use it, how to question its responses and, most importantly, when to rely on your own knowledge and judgement. AI could make us better at what we do, not make us dependent on it. Whether you are writing an article, preparing a presentation or exploring an unfamiliar subject, AI can help you identify relevant topics, explain complex ideas and suggest areas worth investigating. sports.description: Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning celebrates after beating Mississippi at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) Texas football would qualify for the College Football Playoff if the regular season ended before this weekend's slate of games. The Longhorns won the game 17-27. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) Steve Sarkisian 's team dropped two games in October to unranked opponents in Oklahoma and Florida . The defeats make Texas one of six two-loss teams in the current 12-team playoff field, a number that will likely grow in the coming weeks. Ten two-loss teams have qualified for the College Football Playoff across the last two years. Its rare to see a three-loss playoff team, however, with the only two exceptions (Clemson in 2024 and Alabama in 2025) being teams that played in their conference championship game. But will a third loss this season knock Sarkisian and Co. out of the the Playoff? >And what games should Texas fans be on the lookout for this week? Texas has simple route to CFP qualification Let's not complicate matters. Win each of the next three games, and Texas is effectively guaranteed CFP inclusion. The Longhorns' seeding would then be the biggest question, one with multiple potential answers. Texas could close the regular season with wins over LSU, Arkansas and Texas A&M and still miss the SEC championship, then reach the CFP as a 10-2 at-large selection. Being an at-large team likely mean Texas would host a first-round game or hit the road for one. UT would, of course, qualify for the CFP if it did make and win the SEC championship, a scenario in which the Longhorns would then likely receive a top-four seed and subsequent first-round bye. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. Ciryl Gane Explains How His UFC 285 Loss to Jon Jones Fueled His Comeback At UFC 285 in March 2023, Jones made his long-awaited heavyweight debut after nearly four years away from competition. He still understands why LeBron James would use his influence to help his son get there. In Martin’s view, any parent in LeBron’s position would do the same, even if Bronny would have benefited from another season at USC. Speaking on the TFU podcast , Martin addressed the criticism that has followed Bronny since the Los Angeles Lakers selected him with the No. 55 pick in the 2024 NBA Draft. Martin said that he did not question the influence of James’ name, but he also questioned why parents would pass on the chance to influence their own child’s future. “With Bronny and LeBron, yes, nepotism is real. We all know it and we all would do it. If we had the opportunity to do it, 1000%. If any one of us are able to put our child in a position to succeed and have direct influence on it, we would. No doubt about it.” “Do I think Bronny at the time was ready for the NBA? No. Because of his lack of college experience that he had. It was interrupted because of the heart thing. Would loved to have seen him at USC another year to just get playing time. Get used to being back on the floor without all the pressures of what came with making that decision to being in the NBA, and your last name being James.” “And without all the pressures and scrutiny of everything that came with being the 55th pick in the NBA draft, which no other 55th pick has those kind of expectations. We get it. His last name is James, but it’s unfair to the kid. He’s still a kid. But it’s their family. It’s their decision and wish them nothing but the best.” Bronny suffered a cardiac arrest at a USC practice before the season even began. sports.title: Malik Nabers Shuts Down Broadcast Critics With Raw Honesty
sports.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Malik Nabers refused to let a TV crew define his character after Sunday’s win. The Giants wide receiver called the broadcast critique a “lie” and said he will keep speaking his mind. Calling Out the Narrative Fox play-by-play man Joe Davis and analyst Greg Olsen spent time talking about Nabers during the game. They pointed to his reaction on the sideline and claimed his body language was poor. Nabers saw this on social media and decided to strike back. “I just feel like the narrative on me is always all the bad body language things that people have been saying,” Nabers said in comments reported by the New York Post . He said he will not change his behavior to please strangers watching from home. The criticism came after a tough first half where the Giants struggled to score. Nabers spiked his helmet when his team only managed field goals. His streak of four straight 100-yard games ended in that contest, leaving him with 43 yards on five catches. “One thing about it is that I’m an ultimate competitor whether it’s going [well] or if it’s going bad,” Nabers told reporters per the New York Post. He said his intense style comes from a deep passion for the sport, not anger, and he expects others to share that passion. A Direct Challenge to Olsen The former NFL tight end Greg Olsen suggested Nabers was unhappy for teammate Isaiah Likely after a touchdown. Olsen implied Nabers was not a good teammate because of how he carried himself on the field. Nabers rejected this idea entirely and said he has never been called a bad teammate before. “I feel like that was just a lie, attacking my character as a football player and as a teammate,” Nabers stated according to ESPN . He noted that he holds everyone to a high standard of playing “mean” and getting the team fired up. Nabers said he would welcome a simple conversation with Olsen if the analyst wants to talk. He wants to clear the air but will not apologize for his competitiveness. “If he wants to reach out, he can reach out. We can have a civil conversation,” Nabers said per the New York Post. The Giants star emphasized that no one else can speak for him, so he must use his own voice to set the record straight. Focus Shifts to Washington The Giants (5-2-1) hold first place in their division after beating the Eagles 19-11. Nabers said he is already moving past the broadcast drama to focus on the next opponent. He mentioned that the long year of rehab he endured to return from a torn ACL, fuels his drive this season. The team now prepares for a Thursday night game against the Washington Commanders. That matchup is set for Thursday, Nov. 12, at 8:15 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium.

sports.description: Harry Kane will set a new England record of 126 appearances when he features in a Nations League match against Croatia at Wembley (John Walton) England captain Harry Kane said breaking the Three Lions' appearance record in Thursday's Nations League clash with Croatia will represent a "testament to all the dedication" that has gone into his career. When Kane leads England out at Wembley to earn his 126th cap, he will surpass the previous record held by former goalkeeper Peter Shilton since 1990. It will be the latest landmark in an incredible 12 months for the Bayern Munich striker, who in October became the first English player in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or. The 33-year-old Kane is also England's record scorer with 91 goals, as well as holding Tottenham Hotspur's all-time mark with 280. Since leaving Spurs to join Bayern in 2023, Kane has taken his game to another level. He has amassed 156 goals for the German club, finally winning the first silverware of his career with Bundesliga titles in 2025 and 2026. But breaking Shilton's long-standing record also matters to Kane, who told a pre-match press conference on Wednesday: "It's definitely up there as the biggest (achievement). "I think it showcases consistency at the highest level. Testament to all the dedication, the time people don't see that keeps me fit and healthy. This is one of the biggest milestones in my career." For all Kane's brilliance, England have not won a major men's international trophy since lifting the 1966 World Cup on home soil. And Kane suffered fresh frustration in July as England were beaten by Argentina in the semi-finals of the World Cup. - 'Beautiful occasion' - England were leading 1-0 until late in the game but could not score again, with manager Thomas Tuchel criticised for packing the team's defence only for Argentina to score twice late on as Kane was denied a first appearance in a World Cup final. "In terms of what's next, I don't like to put limits -- 100 goals (for England) is a milestone to reach as soon as possible," added Kane. "We've done extremely well in tournaments, going into latter stages. I'm feeling really good and hopefully there will be many more years to see what I can achieve." Tuchel, speaking earlier Wednesday, was coy when asked if Kane was England's greatest footballer. "I don't know. He's up there of course. It's now proven. It's always nice if things are proven in sports -- he has his prizes and records, he will build on these records, score more goals and get more games. "Tomorrow he will start for us and as captain. It's a big occasion to present the Ballon d'Or trophy to our fans and have it embedded in the same day he gets his all-time record for 126 matches, it's a beautiful occasion." England are all but guaranteed a place in March's Nations League quarter-finals, regardless of Thursday's result, having thrashed Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka last month in what Tuchel labelled a "freak result". sports.description: Earning the top seed is one thing. Living up to the expectations that come with it is another. And on Tuesday, St. Mary's volleyball offered another reminder of why its program has claimed five Northern California championships, 14 Sac-Joaquin Section titles and 32 league championships. One week after a CIF Sac-Joaquin Section semifinal loss , top-seeded St. Mary's bounced back with a dramatic CIF State Division II first-round victory over No. 16 Cardinal Newman, the North Bay-Oak League's first-place finisher, at Anthony Morelli Gym, 19-25, 25-16, 25-17, 22-25, 15-13. "We weren't at our best," St. Mary's coach Garren Allala said. "But sometimes you have to find a way to hold on, stick with it and be resilient. You can't blink. Sometimes it's OK to win ugly, and I'm glad we got it out of the way now." For a St. Mary's team that finished the regular season with 80 consecutive Tri-City Athletic League victories, the fifth set brought a different kind of challenge. The Rams trailed 11-9 and later 13-12 before pulling out the win. "I was a little stressed for a while there," senior outside hitter Shea Hardcastle said. "I couldn't breathe for a second. I'm just so happy for us. We pulled through. God's got us." Through it all, junior libero and UC Santa Barbara commit Rachel Nemee was doing what Allala has come to call her "the backbone" for. Willing to put her body on the line and do the dirty work, Nemee finished with a career-high 38 digs. That brought her career total to 1,126, setting a St. Mary's school record. "I didn't even know until the very end," Nemee said. "I just broke down in tears. I'm so happy. I'm going to put that record so far out of reach. I want to keep it forever, like to the grave. This program has been so special to me, and it wouldn't be possible without the girls beside me." And those girls had plenty to do with it. Then there was Nevaeh Wells, who seemed to play just about every position except libero with 11 kills, 18 digs and 26 assists. "Our fight's always going to show through defense," Allala said. "We always say, whatever happens, don't lose our identity. We lost our minds a little bit and some of that identity, but we embraced the moment and stayed in it." It features a tandem OLED screen that stacks two layers of organic light-emitting pixels, eliminating the need for a backlight, and adds touch capability to the MacBook line for the first time. Although the vendor was patted on the back in recent years for improving the repairability of its famously locked-down products, this machine shows Apple still has some way to go. The good? The entire lid comes off relatively easily. Its three-screw hinges closely resemble those on the M6 14-inch MacBook Pro, while streamlined display cable brackets simplify removal. Apple's Repair Assistant tool also handled a full system board swap well. Despite concerns about Touch ID fingerprint authentication, everything went relatively smoothly when iFixit paired a touchscreen from one machine with a logic board from another. On the first boot, Repair Assistant recognized the battery, display, and Touch ID sensor, and touch control needed no separate calibration. The bad? Replacing the panel alone is not possible. When iFixit tried to separate it from the lid, the glass delaminated, cracking the OLED and touch-sensitive layers beneath. That could make for a costlier repair than bargained for. Under the bottom cover, the PROLED has a similar internal layout to the last few models of MacBook Pros, with the fans, board, speakers, and trackpad all in the same places. That means the same annoyances persist. The MagSafe power connector can be removed via two screws and a bracket, yet the USB-C ports can't be extracted the same way because the logic board is in the way. The headphone jack and the fans also require removing the system board first, and the HDMI port and SDXC card reader are soldered to the board itself, as is the storage and memory. Another gripe is that this MacBook's battery pack is hard to remove, though at least it is removable, unlike in many thin-and-light laptops. The tested Pro weighs 1.38 kg or about 3 pounds. For these reasons, the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display earns a 5 out of 10 repairability score from iFixit , but this is actually a one point increase over the score it gave the M5 MacBook Pro. The Apple logo has its own lighting. Older MacBooks with illuminated logos borrowed light from the LCD backlight shining through an apple-shaped window in the lid. This model uses a strip of LEDs along one edge of the logo, passing through a diffuser for an even glow. Because it sits behind the display panel, it would be nearly impossible to repair if it failed, especially if the panel is destroyed during removal. technology.title: Microsoft's Patch Tuesday can't break stuff if it won't install
technology.description: Users are having difficulty installing Microsoft's latest Windows patch. Patch Tuesday contained a truckload of fixes for Microsoft products . However, for some users, installing the update, KB5132061, is proving challenging. In the hours after the patch was released, multiple complaints began to surface that the download and installation were failing, with some customers reporting a 0x800F0993 error code. Others say they received a 0x800F0989 error. Microsoft does not currently list any known issues with the update and is yet to make a statement or provide explanation for the glitch. In addition to the security fixes, this patch resolves a number of known issues from previous updates, including a problem where USB Audio 1.0 devices might fail to start and display an error code 10 in Device Manager. In the absence of a statement from Microsoft, several users have taken to sleuthing. One, with the handle of Forceflow on the ElevenForum site, suggested the bug might be related to Windows Sandbox, and said that after disabling the feature and rebooting, the patch installed successfully. However, others reported problems regardless of Windows Sandbox status, and alternative solutions included using DISM (Deployment Image Servicing and Management) to check the package or downloading the update manually. It's an important patch to install, since it addresses 726 vulnerabilities in Windows alone, and the difficulties affected users face are less than ideal. Microsoft patches have lately displayed more gremlins than usual. Out-of-band releases are depressingly regular after updates break functionality. A September Out-of-band release, for example, was hurriedly pushed out after the September 2026 Windows security update caused trouble for Remote Desktop Services. The October Patch Tuesday for Windows Server sent Exchange Servers toppling , with a registry edit workaround suggested. There was no out-of-band update - Microsoft said the problem had been resolved in the November update. At least this latest release appears to be failing before users get a chance to see what is broken this time. The Register has asked Microsoft to comment. ®

technology.title: NASA asks Earthlings to wave as Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away
technology.description: Voyager 1 will become the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth next week, and NASA wants us to mark the occasion by flashing our lights at the sky. The spacecraft, which suffered a communications hiccup last month, is traveling at approximately 38,000 mph (61,000 kph) and will mark the 50th anniversary of its launch next year. Before then, it has another distance record to set. "Light-day" is a bit snappier than 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers). NASA puts the crossing at 05:16:07 EST (10:16:07 UTC) on Wednesday, November 18. For "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day," participants are invited to flash the mission's three-letter designation – VGR – in Morse code after sunset on November 17, using a flashlight or NASA's website. According to the space agency, this will create "a symbolic wave of golden light encircling the planet after sunset." It is also a nice way to mark the achievement – Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object from Earth, and its extraordinary longevity remains a testament to the skill of engineers past and present. Not that Voyager 1 will be able to detect any flashlights on Earth. Its cameras were turned off decades ago, after the famous Pale Blue Dot image was captured. NASA has invited the public to join in a spacecraft photo opportunity before. On July 19, 2013, Cassini photographed Earth and the Moon from its orbit around Saturn for "The Day the Earth Smiled," while people back home were encouraged to look up and "just smile at the sheer joy of being alive on a Pale Blue Dot." Voyager 2, the spacecraft's sibling, is not expected to reach the same milestone for another nine years. It took a different path through the solar system to swing past Uranus and Neptune. It will, however, be uncertain as to whether Voyager 2 will still be able to communicate by then – even with recent efforts to eke out the probe's dwindling power supply, margins are razor thin. ®

technology.description: Google DeepMind researchers used agentic AI to mathematically prove, or “formally verify,” a number of the Signal protocol’s key cryptographic guarantees—a landmark development for the widely used cryptography and AI itself. Conducted as a sort of proof-of-concept project in just four weeks, the work is significant in two ways. It serves as further independent validation of the cryptography that protects massive quantities of the world's communications on platforms like the Signal app , Google Messages, and WhatsApp. And it demonstrates Google DeepMind's formal verification capabilities using a new AI framework called AlphaProof Code. More broadly, AI-aided formal verification is having a moment, but it is unclear how practical it will be for widespread use and how effective it can be at securing large amounts of code. Proponents of formal verification have long referred to it as a sort of holy grail in software security, because it uses math to check and validate that software is functioning as intended—in other words, that it doesn't have critical vulnerabilities. technology.title: 2013 breach at Russian cybercrime forum resurfaces with millions of victims' credentials
technology.description: A 2013 breach of Russian-language cybercrime forum YouHack exposed its members' login details – and millions of credentials they had posted about other victims, according to newly cataloged data. Have I Been Pwned (HIBP) added the breach on Wednesday, recording 7.2 million unique email addresses. Around 107,000 belonged to forum members, whose exposed data included usernames, IP addresses, and mostly unsalted MD5 password hashes. Unsalted MD5 is a poor choice for protecting passwords. It's fast to compute, allowing attackers to test guesses at speed, and identical passwords produce identical hashes. Hardly good hygiene for a hacking forum. You might expect members of a cybercrime forum to know better than to reuse passwords or register with an email address tied to their real identity. Expectations and reality are not always on speaking terms, as AlphaBay founder Alexandre Cazes demonstrated. YouHack, a longtime cybercrime forum, moved to a different domain after the 2013 breach and remains active, giving cybercrims a place to trade stolen credentials and financial data. The data collated from that digital burglary was eventually bundled into 2024's so-called Mother of all Breaches – a 12TB, 26 billion-record mega-dump of files taken from myriad data security lapses. Millions more HIBP separately published its findings concerning another Russian data breach today. It said the 2023 breach of Russian bank Sberbank's loyalty program (SberSpasibo) contained records belonging to 48 million users. The dataset included 3.3 million unique email addresses, alongside phone numbers and dates of birth. Bank card numbers were stored as unsalted SHA-1 hashes, which could let attackers test possible numbers against the leaked hashes for a match. Reporting on the SberSpasibo breach at the time suggested the records were dated between April 2017 and February 2022, and the attack was claimed by the pro-Ukraine hacktivist outfit NLB. NLB also claimed responsibility for an attack on Sberbank's internal systems at the same time, and later took partial credit for an attack on Alfa-Bank , Russia's largest private bank. ®

technology.title: Shipping giant Maersk probes 'IT security incident,' data theft
technology.description: Shipping behemoth A.P. Moller-Maersk says it is investigating "an IT security incident" involving the potential theft of data from a legacy system. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the Denmark-based shipping, cargo, and logistics giant confirmed it immediately launched an investigation into the attack and the affected system was secured. "Our findings so far strongly suggest no sensitive data has been disclosed," the company said . "The incident is isolated to a local system, and we have found no indication that there has been any impact on other Maersk systems or customer and partner systems that connect to Maersk through integrations such as APIs and EDI." Maersk described the legacy local system as one "from a previous acquisition," and said it does not expect the attack to have an effect on operations. Customers were reassured that they can continue to use Maersk platforms to manage their shipments as usual, and to expect updates from the company as and when they're available. "Cybersecurity remains a constant, ongoing priority for Maersk," it added. "We have rigorous processes in place to identify and prevent incidents and minimize customer impact. "As always, please treat any unexpected communications claiming to relate to this matter with caution and verify them through your usual Maersk contact. "Thank you for your patience as we continue to investigate the incident." Fortunately for those who immediately feel uneasy after hearing "Maersk" and "IT security" mentioned in the same breath, the wording of the shipping giant's disclosure suggests this intrusion won't be as calamitous as the NotPetya disaster in 2017. Mimicking the Petya ransomware strain, NotPetya was an infamous destructive wiper malware strain that wormed its way across the global economy. Western intelligence agencies attributed the malware to Russia's Sandworm group, an outfit believed to be part of the country's military intelligence service (GRU). Maersk said at the time that it expected the attack to result in a circa $300 million bill , owing to remediation and rebuild costs. Offering a sense of scale, Jim Hagemann Snabe, then chair of Maersk, told World Economic Forum delegates in 2018 that the company's rebuild encompassed 4,000 new servers, 45,000 new PCs, and 2,500 applications – which he said had been completed over just ten days. In 2020, as exclusively revealed by The Register , Maersk went on to lay off around 150 staffers from its command and control center in Maidenhead, England. The staffers who lost their jobs had played key roles in the recovery. ®

science.title: Hubble Space Telescope reveals glittering stars with mysterious origins | Space photo of the day for Nov. 11, 2026
science.description: null The Hubble Space Telescope has captured a breathtaking view of thousands of stars glittering like cosmic jewels in a dazzling display of blue, gold and orange. But this spectacular scene is far more than just a pretty picture. Some of these stars are almost as old as the universe itself and could hold clues to how our Milky Way formed. M30 is a globular star cluster located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth. (Image credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, M. Libralato, G. Piotto, A. Sarajedini) What is it? The exquisite image released by ESA on Nov. 5 shows Messier 30 (M30), a densely packed collection of stars located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth in the constellation Capricornus. M30 is a globular cluster, a roughly spherical collection of tens of thousands to millions of stars held together by gravity . Our Milky Way is home to at least 150 of these ancient stellar gatherings, some of which are estimated to be between 11.5 billion and 13.5 billion years old. For comparison, the universe itself is approximately 13.8 billion years old! Why is it amazing Besides looking like a vast cosmic treasure trove glittering across the universe, M30 also has a fascinating story to tell. Globular clusters are essentially cosmic time capsules. Their ancient stars preserve chemical clues about the conditions that existed when they formed, helping astronomers piece together the Milky Way's early history. Astronomers have also discovered that M30, along with several other globular clusters, traverses the Milky Way in the opposite direction to the galaxy's rotation. This unusual motion raises the intriguing possibility that M30 may not have formed in our galaxy at all. It could have simply been captured by the Milky Way billions of years ago.

science.title: NASA's new UVEX space telescope will peer deep into the universe's most violent events
science.description: null A new NASA space telescope will study the universe in ultraviolet light to reveal the violent and turbulent events that bubble under what appears to be a cosmic sea of tranquility. The Ultraviolet Explorer (UVEX) mission, developed by NASA in conjunction with the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), will be the first mission to create deep all-sky maps in ultraviolet light. Thus, when it launches in 2031, UVEX will join new sky-mapping surveys like NASA's SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer), which scans the cosmos in infrared, and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which does the same over the southern hemisphere in visible light, in creating deep-sky maps across a broad swathe of the electromagnetic spectrum. UVEX's ultraviolet views will reveal explosive events such as the collisions between ultra-dense stellar corpses called neutron stars and the supernova explosions that mark the deaths of massive stars and the births of neutron stars and black holes. Additionally, the NASA ultraviolet telescope should be able to detect a multitude of low-mass galaxies much closer to the Milky Way than similar galaxies that are currently being observed millions and even billions of light-years away by NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) . The $590 million UVEX mission will "advance fundamental frontiers in astrophysics, from understanding the smallest galaxies to diagnosing the aftermath of neutron-star mergers and other cosmic explosions," the mission's principal investigator, Caltech physics professor Fiona Harrison, said in an Oct. 27 statement . "The first major ultraviolet space mission in two decades, UVEX is a bold leap forward in our exploration of the ultraviolet universe," Caltech President Ray Jayawardhana said in the same statement. UVEX will paint a picture of cosmic life, death and afterlife UVEX will benefit from a major leap forward in UV sensitivity thanks to its Caltech-built sensors, which are based on complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) imaging technology. This will help the spacecraft tap into what Harrison described as "the untapped opportunity in the UV." UVEX will be uniquely poised to spot millions of nearby, small, and faint galaxies that are teeming with infant stars that emit bright UV light. "In optical light, it's very hard to distinguish these nearby galaxies from faraway ones that look similar," Harrison said. "UV light will make them easier to find." UVEX won't just be investigating the infancy of stars , however. It will also examine the deaths of ancient stars in the form of supernovas. The supernova relic Pa 30, as seen by the Gemini north telescope. (Image credit: International Gemini Observatory/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA) Supernovas occur when a massive star runs out of fuel for nuclear fusion and can no longer support itself against the inward push of its own gravity. science.title: Why I recommend the Seestar S30 Plus smart telescope for beginners — full review
science.description: null I’ve used several smart telescopes over the last few years, but I'd recommend the ZWO Seestar S30 Plus to almost anyone wanting to get started in astrophotography. At $499/€499, it’s a complete imaging system that can photograph galaxies, nebulae and star clusters automatically, even from a light-polluted city. Better still, it’s so small that it can live on a bookshelf. The Pleiades (M45), photographed in mosaic mode with the Seestar S30 Plus. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) Jamie Carter The Andromeda Galaxy (M31) photographed using the Seestar S30 Plus. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) Jamie Carter The Dumbbell Nebula (M27) photographed using the Seestar S30 Plus. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) Jamie Carter I recently captured images of the Dumbbell Nebula (M27), the North America Nebula (NGC 7000), the Andromeda Galaxy (M31) and the Pleiades (M45) with the S30 Plus. All were remarkably easy to capture, and none of the images accompanying this review required external processing. It’s basically point-and-shoot astrophotography — if you live under light-polluted skies, that’s a game-changer. Star trails photographed using the Seestar S30 Plus’s dedicated Star Trail mode. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) (Image credit: Jamie Carter) I also think the S30 Plus makes an ideal companion to a conventional optical telescope. I can set it to photograph a nebula I have no hope of seeing under light pollution while I try to find brighter objects through the eyepiece of another telescope. It will then get on with collecting photons while I enjoy observing. For anyone who already owns a telescope but doesn’t want the expense and complexity of conventional astrophotography, that’s a compelling proposition. I photographed nebulas despite light pollution The S30 Plus is Seestar’s new entry-level smart telescope. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) (Image credit: Jamie Carter) One problem with buying a cheap optical telescope is that deep-sky objects rarely resemble the colorful photographs you see online. The moon, planets and bright star clusters can look wonderful through an eyepiece, but faint galaxies and nebulas are much harder to appreciate, particularly from a town or city. Like all smart telescopes, the S30 Plus gets around that problem by photographing objects rather than showing them directly. Its camera takes repeated exposures, which the telescope automatically stacks to reduce noise and gradually reveal faint detail. The longer you leave it working, the better the resulting image tends to become. Being able to photograph colorful nebulas without traveling to a remote observing site is one of the biggest attractions of the S30 Plus. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 10, 2013: Europe's GOCE satellite, the 'Ferrari of space,' fell out of orbit after mapping Earth's gravity field
science.description: null On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. GOCE, its name was short for Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer, launched in 2009 on a mission to map Earth's gravity like never before. But despite that successful mission, it was doomed in 2013 when it ran out of fuel . At the time, controllers weren't sure where GOCE would fall back to Earth . Some people worried that it might crash into a populated area. However, the small spacecraft broke up in the atmosphere and didn't cause any property damage. It disintegrated about 50 miles above the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. The European Space Agency called the mission a success. GOCE lasted far longer than expected. It showed small variations in Earth's gravity , mapped the structure of Earth's crust and mantle, and tracked ocean currents. Artist's rendering of the "Ferrari of space," the European Space Agency's Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer (GOCE), before it fell from space in 2013. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Why it mattered The GOCE satellite was a sleek spacecraft, with fins covered in solar panels that gave it a futuristic design. In fact, its look earned it a pretty cool nickname. "GOCE's sleek, elegant aerodynamic design — responsible for it being dubbed the 'Ferrari of space' — immediately set it apart from most other satellites,." ESA officials said in a description . There was more than looks behind GOCE's design. In order to generate the best map ever of Earth's gravitational field, GOCE had to fly in an orbit so low — just 139 miles (224 kilometers) — it needed to counteract the drag from the gossamer thin atmosphere of Earth at that altitude. The International Space Station orbits Earth at nearly twice that altitude. GOCE was powered by an xenon ion engine that allowed to maintain its low orbit for four years. Once it ran out of fuel, the 1-ton satellite could not maintain its position in space , leading to a fiery plunge to Earth. The large size of GOCE — it weighed 2,425 pounds (1,100 kilograms) and was 17 feet (5.3 meters) long and 3.2 feet (1 m) wide — made its reentry stand out, particularly since at least 25% of the satellite was expected to reach the Earth's surface .
